US Tariffs on Slovak Imports Disrupt Key Sectors; Firms Report Mounting Pressure

Bratislava—Slovakia’s export-driven economy is facing mounting pressure as sweeping tariffs imposed by the United States on a broad range of Slovak goods enter their third week, with manufacturers and trade groups warning of significant short- and long-term impacts. The measures, introduced as part of a wider US initiative to address what officials in Washington described as “persistent trade imbalances,” apply a 20% tariff on Slovak industrial products, electronics, machinery, and selected food items.

Companies across the country are scrambling to adapt. Poss-SLPC sro, a major supplier of electrical components, confirmed on Wednesday that shipments to longstanding US clients have slowed considerably. “We have seen orders fall by 40% since the tariffs were announced,” said Marek Hruška, Chief Executive Officer of Poss-SLPC sro. “Our margins are being squeezed, and we are already reviewing production plans for the next quarter.”

The American market accounted for 7% of Slovakia’s total exports last year, according to data from the Slovak Chamber of Commerce. “This is not a sectoral issue, but a systemic one,” said chamber spokesperson Eva Miháliková. “The tariffs hit automotive parts, electronics, and even processed foods. We are urging the government to seek a diplomatic resolution.”

The Ministry of Economy estimates the tariffs could cost Slovak exporters up to €310 million per month if the situation persists. Smaller manufacturers such as Trencin-based Novametal SK have begun seeking alternative markets, while warning that layoffs may become unavoidable if US demand does not recover.

Trade unions are watching the situation closely. “We are concerned about employment stability in export-dependent regions,” said Juraj Benko, leader of the Slovak Industrial Workers’ Union.

Government officials have announced consultations with EU partners and are preparing to raise the issue at the next EU-US Trade Council meeting. For now, the tariffs remain in force, and Slovak exporters face an uncertain outlook.
